name: 2000 NIST Speaker Recognition Evaluation (CALLHOME diarization set)
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Obtaining it needs an LDC licence (fee shown after login)
license_note: LDC user agreement. Maintainer decision 2026-10-30: used for evaluation only (internal), like rt03_eval. If callhome_american_english is used for training, check first that it shares no calls or speakers with this set
notes: This row is the CALLHOME part of the speaker segmentation test of the 2000 NIST SRE, released as LDC2001S97. Evaluation plan (catalogue documentation): summed two-channel CALLHOME conversations in a variety of languages, up to 10 minutes and up to 10 speakers each, no more than 500 segments, on discs sid00sg1 and sid00sg2; speakers differ from those of the detection and tracking segments. The whole release (catalogue): 10,328 single-channel SPHERE files, 148.9 hours, mostly Switchboard-2; 1,426 missing files were added on 2017-06-27. The plan forbade training on the CALLHOME corpora for this evaluation, apart from the CALLHOME development CD

name: Third DIHARD Speech Diarization Challenge data
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Two LDC releases: development LDC2022S12 (not checked yet) and evaluation LDC2022S14
license_note: LDC user agreement. Internal use only, never redistributed. Maintainer decisions 2026-10-31: the development set (LDC2022S12) is used for training and the evaluation set (LDC2022S14) for evaluation only. Not checked: whether the two sets share speakers or source recordings (both draw on the same domains, e.g. LibriVox, ADOS, restaurants). The releases reuse audio from other corpora with their own copyrights (catalogue Copyright sections)
notes: Two LDC releases, development LDC2022S12 and evaluation LDC2022S14, of 5-10 minute samples from 11 domains (paper 4.1). The challenge had no training set and no constraints on training data (paper 1). Evaluation set sources (LDC2022S14): ADOS clinical interviews, restaurant conversations, DCIEM/HCRC map task (LDC96S38), Digital Archive of Southern Speech (LDC2012S03), LibriVox audiobooks, 2001 ROAR meeting speech, 2001 U.S. Supreme Court arguments, Mixer 6 Speech (LDC2013S03), VAST video, YouthPoint radio. Development set sources (LDC2022S12) include Fisher CTS, LibriVox, RT-04S meeting speech (LDC2007S11, LDC2007S12) and Supreme Court arguments. The CTS recordings are unreleased Fisher English Phase II calls (paper 4.1). Overlap to check: Mixer 6, LibriVox (the source of LibriSpeech) and Fisher

name: Dinner Party Corpus (DiPCo)
status_note: Deferred: the download given in the paper (s3.amazonaws.com/dipco/DiPCo.tgz) answered 403 AccessDenied on 2026-10-31. Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Becomes candidate once a working copy or source is confirmed
notes: Recorded by Amazon with groups of four employee volunteers in one room; 39 time-synchronised microphones per session (4 headsets + 5 devices x 7 channels), 16 kHz WAV downsampled from 45 kHz (paper 2.2). 32 adult speakers aged 22-62, 19 male, 13 female. Sessions last 15-47 minutes and include music playback from a given time mark (Table 3). Sessions S09/S10 and S06/S07 have the same participants. The close-talk recording of P13 in S04 is noisier (2.3). Transcribers ignored other speakers on each close-talk channel, so overlapping speech is labelled per speaker. Designed after CHiME-5 (2.3)

name: DISPLACE 2023
status_note: Only the Dev set is published (Zenodo, CC BY 4.0, 1.58 GB). No release of the Eval set was found. Not on the lab's shared corpus storage
language_note: Named in the paper for Dev and Eval Phase-1: Hindi, Kannada, Bengali, Malayalam, Telugu, Tamil and Indian-accented English, with code-mixing (language labels per word). The full Eval set adds languages not named
license_note: Dev set: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo record 8375161). Eval set: terms unknown, not found
notes: Recorded at two Indian academic institutes in rooms without soundproofing, with a lapel microphone per speaker and one far-field omnidirectional desktop microphone; conversations of 30-60 minutes; 16 kHz (paper 3.1-3.2). RTTM covers both speaker and language diarization. Participants are 33% female, mostly aged 17-40. Evaluation was run in two phases (Phase-1: 20 recordings, 11.5 h; Phase-2: the full Eval set)

name: Earnings-21
status_note: Not on the lab's shared corpus storage (earnings22 is, as segmented audio; it is a different dataset). Downloadable from GitHub with Git LFS
license_note: Text only: transcripts and associated text files under CC BY-SA 4.0 (earnings21/LICENSE.md). Audio: no licence; the 44 calls were downloaded from Seeking Alpha and are distributed on a fair-use claim (paper footnote 3). Maintainer decision 2026-10-31: evaluation only, as the dataset was built as an ASR evaluation benchmark (RTTM added for DER evaluation); never used for training
notes: RTTM for all 44 recordings was added to the repository on 2023-12-05 (rttms/, for DER evaluation); for 4341191 and 4363614 a human re-transcribed the speaker labels, so their RTTM differs from the transcripts. Recordings last 17 min to 1 h 34 min at 11.025-44.1 kHz (paper Table 1). 9 sectors from Seeking Alpha; speaker names in speaker-metadata.csv where transcriptionists gave them. Intended as an ASR evaluation benchmark; the paper has no train/test split

name: Ego4D
status_note: Needs a signed Ego4D licence agreement (maintainer decision). Not on the lab's shared corpus storage. Only the AV diarization (AVD) benchmark has speaker segments; its annotations come with the Ego4D annotations download (about 2 GB), its clips with the benchmark clips
language_note: Not stated for the AVD clips. Transcription covers only English speakers in this version (AV diarization page), which implies other languages occur
license_note: Ego4D licence agreement, signed by an individual or an institution (ego4d-data.org Start Here). Its terms were not read: the agreement page answered HTTP 429 on 2026-10-31. The EGO4D/audio-visual repository is code under MIT; that licence does not cover the data
notes: Ego4D: 3,670 hours of daily-life egocentric video from 931 camera wearers in 74 locations and 9 countries; only portions have audio (paper abstract). Diarization labels exist only for the Audio-Visual Diarization (AVD) benchmark (github.com/EGO4D/audio-visual): about 50 h annotated out of >750 h of conversational data, 572 clips of 5 minutes, on average 4.71 speakers per clip and 0.74 per frame, the camera wearer speaking 77.64 s per clip (README). Annotations: face boxes, active speaker labels, voice_segments per person, English transcripts. 2022 challenges on eval.ai: audio-video and audio-only diarization
